structure.title: [MMD老人们](https://archive.is/o/uzBzp/https://tottotoittoiee.hatenablog.com/entry/2022/08/16/105314)
structure.prefix_summary: The document critiques the MikuMikuDance (MMD) community by questioning the notion that MMD is “easy” or accessible due to endorsement by long-retired users. The author argues that advanced techniques like Ray-mmd and sdPBR have increased difficulty, while other creators migrate to sophisticated tools such as Cinema4D, Blender, or Unreal Engine. They highlight dwindling motivation within the community, describing past trends as fleeting and lacking sustained mainstream appeal. They conclude that MMD’s ease can yield homogeneous results, contributing to the platform’s decline.

nodes.summary: The document reflects on nostalgic views of the MMD community’s past vibrancy, acknowledging that in the heat of enthusiasm people lose perspective. It explores how various individuals perceive MMD’s decline and attempted revival, referencing discussions about decreasing participation. Through a reflective tone, the author highlights concerns about platform limitations, community fragmentation, and external influences that resemble intrusions or disruptions. There is commentary on the risks of relying on ambiguous security claims or commercial-use restrictions, especially when comparing MMD with more established tools like game engines and DCC software, questioning the feasibility of such alternatives without a stable foundation.

It discusses debates about whether MMD creators should ban certain software or add usage restrictions, particularly for creating content in Blender, Unreal Engine, or VR. The text draws comparisons to other tools such as Unity and discusses skepticism toward those who fixate on outdated platforms instead of embracing game engines. Quotes from forum threads and blog comments illustrate how community members disagree over rendering effort, licensing rules, and the future viability of MMD content.
